grammar.rule_explanation_ru: В клиническом диалоге точные грамматические структуры помогают быстрее понять жалобы пациента.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good afternoon. Please have a seat. What seems to be the problem?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Good afternoon, doctor. I've been having severe pain in my lower right tooth for the last few days. It has become difficult to eat and sleep.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: When did the pain first start, and has it been getting worse recently?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: It started about three days ago, and unfortunately, it has become much worse since yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Does anything make the pain worse, such as chewing or putting pressure on the tooth?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Yes. It hurts a lot when I chew on that side, so I've been trying to use the other side of my mouth.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Let me examine the tooth. I may also need to take an X-ray to see what is happening underneath the gum.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Okay. Do you think the tooth can be saved?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Unfortunately, the tooth is badly damaged, and the infection has affected the surrounding area. In this case, extraction may be the safest option.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I'm a little nervous about having it removed. Will it be painful?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Don't worry. We'll use a local anaesthetic to numb the area. You may feel some pressure during the extraction, but you shouldn't feel any sharp pain.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: How long will the procedure take?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: If everything goes as expected, it should take around 20 to 30 minutes. However, the exact time depends on the position and condition of the tooth.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Is there anything I need to do before the procedure?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Yes. Please tell me if you are taking any medications or if you have any allergies.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: I'm not allergic to any medication, and I'm not taking anything regularly.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Good. I'll give you the local anaesthetic now. Please let me know if you feel any pain during the procedure.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: All right, doctor.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: The tooth has been removed successfully. I'm placing a piece of gauze over the extraction site. Bite down on it firmly for about 30 to 45 minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: What should I avoid after the extraction?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Avoid smoking, drinking alcohol, and eating very hot or hard food for at least the first 24 hours. Also, don't rinse your mouth vigorously because it can disturb the blood clot.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Can I brush my teeth tonight?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Yes, but be very gentle around the extraction site. You should also avoid touching the area with your tongue or fingers.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: What if the pain gets worse later?

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: Some pain and swelling are normal after an extraction. You can take the painkiller I recommend. However, if you develop severe swelling, persistent bleeding, fever, or increasing pain after a few days, contact the clinic immediately.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.text: Thank you, doctor. That makes me feel much more comfortable.

dialogue.speaker: Doctor
dialogue.text: You're welcome. Follow the aftercare instructions carefully, and you should recover well.
